content: The original sample size does not reflect the effective cluster-adjusted sample size used in the meta-analysis. In the meta-analysis conducted by Wray (2018), multiple intervention arms included HIV self-testing (HIVST) with similar kit distribution methods, so these arms were combined. Cluster-adjusted analyses were incorporated for cluster-randomized trials. Four individual randomized trials were included, and the analysis was downgraded twice due to a 4% overall loss to follow-up (LTFU), with 26% in the intervention arm and 50% in the control arm. For example, Patel (2018) reported a 36% overall LTFU, with 44% in the intervention arm and 27% in the control arm. Each trial had more than three domains with high or unclear risks of bias. In Choko (2019a), multiple intervention arms with similar HIVST kit distribution methods were combined. In Choko (2019b), two intervention arms included HIVST and had subgroups (antenatal care [ANC] women and antiretroviral therapy [ART] clients). HIVST arms were combined, but subgroups were presented separately. Five individual randomized trials and three cluster-randomized trials were included, and the analysis was downgraded once due to potential recruitment bias in two cluster-randomized trials. Some bias domains were unclear due to insufficient information from unpublished reports or conference abstracts. In Chanda (2017) and Ortblad (2017), multiple intervention arms included HIVST, but the distribution methods differed, so the arms were not combined. The control arm sample was adjusted to prevent double counting. Three cluster-randomized trials were included, and the analysis was downgraded once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) and detection bias (self-reported or non-validated outcomes) in all trials. One trial had unclear risks of selection bias (allocation concealment), selective reporting, and baseline cluster imbalance. In Jamil (2017), Katz (2018), and MacGowan (2017), three trials were conducted among men who have sex with men (MSM) in high-income countries (Australia and the United States). The analysis was downgraded once due to potential performance bias and unclear detection bias in one trial. Three of the four trials had more than three domains with high or unclear risks of bias. In Kelvin (2019), three-arm randomized controlled trials (RCTs) contributed to the analysis. Enhanced standard of care (SoC) was excluded, and standard SoC was used for comparison with the intervention arm. Chanda (2017) and Ortblad (2017) had multiple intervention arms, but differences in intervention packages likely impacted positivity, so the arms were not pooled. Two individual randomized and one cluster-randomized trial were included, and the analysis was downgraded twice due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) and detection bias in two trials. One trial had unclear risks of selection bias (random sequence generation). In Choko (2019a) and Wray (2018), multiple intervention arms with similar HIVST kit distribution methods were combined. In Choko (2019b), two intervention arms included HIVST, and the ANC group was included in this analysis. Ten individual randomized and three cluster-randomized trials were included. The analysis was downgraded once due to potential recruitment bias in three cluster-randomized trials. Several bias domains were unclear due to insufficient information from unpublished reports or conference abstracts. In Chanda (2017) and Ortblad (2017), only the HIVST arm with facility-based distribution was included. Two individual randomized and two cluster-randomized trials were included. The analysis was downgraded once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) and detection bias in two trials. Two trials had unclear risks of selection bias (random sequence generation and allocation concealment). In Choko (2019b), only the ART group was included in the analysis. One individual randomized and one cluster-randomized trial were included. The analysis was downgraded twice due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) in both trials and detection bias in one trial. One trial had unclear risks of selection bias (random sequence generation and allocation concealment). Both trials had more than three domains with high or unclear risks of bias. In Chanda (2017) and Ortblad (2017), only the HIVST arm with direct distribution to peers was included. Two cluster-randomized trials were included, and the analysis was downgraded once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) and detection bias in both trials. In one cluster-randomized trial, the analysis was downgraded once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) and unclear detection bias (self-reported or non-validated outcomes). In another single trial, the analysis was downgraded once due to inconsistency, as it could not be evaluated. In Choko (2019a), multiple intervention arms with similar HIVST kit distribution methods were combined. Seven individual randomized and six cluster-randomized trials were included. The analysis was downgraded once due to potential recruitment bias in three cluster-randomized trials. Several bias domains were unclear due to insufficient information from unpublished reports or conference abstracts. In Chanda (2017) and Ortblad (2017), only the HIVST arm with direct distribution to peers was included. Two cluster-randomized trials were included, and the analysis was downgraded once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) and detection bias in both trials.
